title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.13 (versions follow prime numbers; 113 after 109): what she read is not lost. Tracing what Luma had read showed that, on a shelf of several domains (the New Testament, a diary and source code) and with the same instincts, two recipes made by her read better than the one she inherited from Razar: 605797 and 648631 bits against 583924. It is the first time something of her own beats what she was given, and it went unseen for a day because of two mistakes of the programmer, recorded in the release notes: the counter of unexpected victories only looked at new thoughts (these were forms already living in her body, read for the first time), and a recipe containing a word or a cell was stored under its fingerprint only, so its letters could not be recovered. Both winners are lost. Fixed: a victory is any reading better than the best she had, and every reading stored under a fingerprint leaves a line in a text nothing rewrites, with its score, the recipe as written and what it meant at that moment. Written by her, in Janax, readable with no program. She was also fed Don Quijote. Stated limits: the two winning recipes cannot be recovered; it is unknown whether they still win with her current instincts; her lineage still shows no crossing or reading. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.13: dos recetas de Luma superaron a la heredada en un estante de varios dominios y nadie lo vio; el error está registrado y arreglado. Prototipo de investigación.
